faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Questions we get asked the most
faq.subtitle: 8 common questions from SMBs. If you don't see yours, just contact us directly.

items.q: We're on a tight budget. Can we still go digital?
items.a: Absolutely. Digital transformation isn't all-or-nothing. We'll recommend the highest-impact module for your budget — start with a company website + basic CRM for as low as ¥3,000. Expand as your business grows. Good solutions aren't afraid of phased delivery.

items.q: What makes you different from a regular outsourcing company?
items.a: Three things. First, we don't just "deliver code" — we're your long-term tech partner with ongoing maintenance and iteration. Second, our stack is modern, open-source, and vendor-independent — the code is yours, deployed on your own cloud account. Third, monthly retainer instead of one-time contracts — pivot anytime. In short: we want to be your external CTO, not a one-and-done vendor.

items.q: Do you provide support after launch?
items.a: Absolutely. Launch is the beginning, not the end. We offer maintenance plans: server monitoring, daily database backups, auto SSL renewal, security scanning, 24/7 incident response. Every client has a dedicated support group — critical issues answered within 30 minutes.

items.q: I don't know tech. How do I explain my needs?
items.a: That's exactly our specialty. We're fluent in translating tech jargon into plain business language. The process is simple: tell us your business pain points (e.g. "sales team quotes wrong prices", "customer info is a mess", "I want to sell online"), and we'll turn them into technical solutions. No requirement doc needed — we'll guide you through it.

items.q: How much time and money for a website or system?
items.a: Depends on scope. Simple company site: 2–4 weeks, ¥3K–8K. Functional web app: 6–12 weeks, ¥15K–50K. Custom ERP/management system: 8–20 weeks, starts at ¥30K. These are reference ranges — after a free consultation, we'll give you a precise quote and timeline.

items.q: What if I want to stop mid-project?
items.a: We work on a monthly retainer — no long-term lock-in. If it's not a fit, give one month's notice. All code, databases, domains, and cloud accounts are your assets. We'll provide handover documentation so anyone can take over. Vendor lock-in is against our principles.

items.q: Can you build WeChat Mini Programs?
items.a: Yes. We do WeChat and Alipay mini-programs, fully integrated with your website and backend — one update, all platforms synced. A common setup: brand website + WeChat mini-program store + unified admin dashboard.

items.q: How do you handle data security?
items.a: All data is stored on Supabase (AWS-backed) or Alibaba Cloud, with automatic daily backups. Full HTTPS encryption in transit. Role-based access control in the admin panel (owner/manager/staff see different data). Row Level Security (RLS) at the database level prevents data leaks. You can export all your data anytime.

items.title: From zero to digital: A manufacturer's 3-year transformation

points.label: Background:
points.text: Shengda is an ¥80M manufacturing company. Customer inquiries relied on phone and WeChat. Order management was Excel-based. 200+ product SKUs meant sales staff frequently quoted the wrong prices.

points.label: Solution:
points.text: Two-phase delivery — Phase 1: company website (product catalog + online inquiry). Phase 2: internal order management system integrated with production scheduling.

points.label: Tech Stack:
points.text: Next.js + Tailwind CSS + Supabase (order database) + Stripe (deposit payments). Deployed on the client's own Alibaba Cloud account.

points.label: Result:
points.text: Online inquiries doubled within 3 months. Information flow between sales and the shop floor went from "WeChat group shouting" to instant system notifications. The client said: "Finally, no more late-night Excel scrolling."

items.title: How an education provider went digital and survived

points.label: Background:
points.text: Zhixing is a mid-sized training center in Zhengzhou. They relied on in-person classes + WeChat groups for materials. During the pandemic, student retention plummeted — they urgently needed an online course system.

points.label: Solution:
points.text: Built an online learning platform supporting video courses, learner progress tracking, and homework submission/grading. Key requirement: non-technical teaching staff must be able to upload courses, schedule classes, and view student data without IT help.

points.label: Tech Stack:
points.text: Next.js App Router + Supabase (student data + video assets) + Server Actions (homework submission). Admin interface built with Tailwind and detailed role-based permissions.

points.label: Result:
points.text: Within 6 months, students grew from 80 offline to 300+ online. Course completion rate jumped from under 40% to 85% — because the system automatically alerts staff when a student is about to fall behind.

items.title: Brand digital upgrade for a retail chain

points.label: Background:
points.text: Xianfeng operates 15 fresh food stores in Luoyang. Previously only had a WeChat Official Account for promotions — no brand website, no unified online store. Each store operated independently, customer data was scattered.

points.label: Solution:
points.text: A brand website showcasing company image + product sourcing stories. Plus a WeChat mini-program store for online ordering with in-store pickup. Unified backend managing products, inventory, and orders across all 15 locations.

points.label: Tech Stack:
points.text: Brand site: pure HTML + Tailwind static (Lighthouse 98). Mini-program store backend: Supabase + Stripe payments. Store management dashboard: Next.js.

points.label: Result:
points.text: Online sales grew 200% within 6 months. SEO on the brand site pushed Xianfeng to top-3 local search results. The owner said: "Customers used to think we were just a vegetable stand. Now we look like a real brand."

items.title: How a trading company stopped managing clients by memory

points.label: Background:
points.text: Hengtong is an import/export trading company. 500+ client contacts were scattered across 6 sales reps' WeChat, Excel spreadsheets, and their own memories. The boss had no idea who was following up on what or which clients were about to be lost.

points.label: Solution:
points.text: First, a company website showcasing credentials and product lines to build trust with overseas buyers. Second, a lightweight CRM — client profiles, follow-up records, quotation management, contract expiration reminders.

points.label: Tech Stack:
points.text: Next.js + Supabase RLS (Row Level Security — each sales rep only sees their own client data). CI/CD via GitHub Actions auto-deploying to Alibaba Cloud.

points.label: Result:
points.text: The boss can now check on his phone "which sales rep hasn't followed up this week." Client data no longer disappears when a sales rep leaves. The website brought in 3 overseas inquiries after launch.
